state.case_summary:
A 48-year-old woman with no breast symptoms underwent routine screening mammography, which demonstrated a new 1.4-cm developing asymmetry in the inner quadrant of the right breast on craniocaudal and mediolateral oblique views. Targeted breast ultrasonography at the 4:00 position, 4 cm from the nipple, showed no discrete abnormality corresponding to the mammographic finding. Because the asymmetry persisted, a tomosynthesis-guided vacuum-assisted biopsy of the right inner breast was performed, yielding 12 core specimens. Histologic examination revealed marked perilobular and periductal mixed chronic inflammatory infiltrate enriched in eosinophils, with lymphocytes and plasma cells and no granulomata. The Allergy and Immunology service noted that the patient was asymptomatic, with no history of urticaria, asthma, angioedema, or pruritus except for seasonal allergic rhinitis. Peripheral blood eosinophil levels were within the normal range. Hypereosinophilic syndrome was excluded from consideration.

Options:

D. Exclusion of Churg
E. Exclusion of systemic allergic eosinophilic disorders (e.g., asthma, urticaria)
